hook: Myth: keep your credit card balance under thirty percent and your score is fine.

blocks.narration: Myth: keep your credit card balance under thirty percent and your score is fine. Fact: lower is usually better.
blocks.visual: A sleek glossy credit card floats above a glowing meter that reads thirty, then slides lower

blocks.narration: Credit utilization means how much of your available credit you are using. It falls under amounts owed, about thirty percent of a FICO score.
blocks.visual: A glass tank labeled with a card icon fills partway with glowing blue liquid

blocks.narration: Thirty percent is not a magic line. Using less of your limit generally looks better to scoring models, not just staying under thirty.
blocks.visual: The liquid level drops step by step while a score dial ticks upward with each step

blocks.narration: People with the very highest scores tend to use only a small slice of their limits, often under ten percent.
blocks.visual: A row of score dials, the highest ones paired with nearly empty glass tanks

blocks.narration: Here is the part most people miss. Card issuers usually report your statement balance, not what you owe after paying the bill.
blocks.visual: A calendar with one date glowing as a snapshot camera flashes at the card

blocks.narration: So even if you pay in full every month, a big statement balance can still show high utilization to the credit bureaus.
blocks.visual: The camera snapshot shows a tall liquid level even though a hand empties the tank right after

blocks.narration: Paying down the balance a few days before the statement closes can lower the number they see. Utilization has no long memory either.
blocks.visual: A hand drains the tank just before the camera flashes, the photo now showing a low level

blocks.narration: Pay early, use less, and your score can respond within a billing cycle or two. Follow for one credit rule a day.
blocks.visual: The score dial climbs into the green zone, glowing particles rising around the card

cta: Follow for one credit rule a day.

captions.hook_line: The '30% rule' is hurting your credit score more than you think 💳
captions.body: Amounts owed make up about 30% of a FICO score, and lower utilization is generally better. Card issuers usually report your statement balance, so paying before the statement closes can lower what the bureaus see.

youtube_title: The 30% Credit Card Rule Is a Myth
